newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says more boatpeople heading for Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says more boatpeople heading for Hong Kong.

text.p: Vietnam's prime minister has ordered a drive to prevent people fleeing the country after evidence that the numbers leaving for Hong Kong has increased, official media reports said on Thursday.
"In recent months, the illegal immigration of Vietnamese into Hong Kong has increased...," the official Vietnam News Agency said, quoting Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet's directive.
So far this year 780 people have fled by boat to Hong Kong, and 32 have stayed on after visiting as tourists, it said.
An official with a foreign non-governmental organisation in Hanoi said many had left because word had spread there were jobs and money to be earned building Hong Kong's new airport.
Hundreds of thousands of Vietnamese fled in flimsy boats in the years after the 1975 communist victory, all of them seeking political asylum, and washed up in countries around the region.
With United Nations funding for camps now at an end, Southeast Asian nations have been forcing home their last asylum seekers.
Those in Hong Kong, now less than 10,000, are all due to be sent home before the British colony reverts to Chinese rule next year.
Migration out of Vietnam has slowed to a dribble and has not been a source of serious concern for the past five years.

However, Kiet said continuing illegal migration to Hong Kong had affected the government's efforts to work together with the administration there and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) on returnees.

The Communist Party daily Nhan Dan said Kiet had ordered the authorities to make people understand that there were no job opportunities in Hong Kong and that leaving the territory was not possible because it will be returned to China in mid-1997.
He also wanted people to understand that the UNHCR no longer provides financial assistance to migrants.
"The Hong Kong authorities will put these people in jail for one to six months and then expel them without any support from the UNHCR," Nhan Dan said.
Kiet also called for heightened control of border areas and speedy coordination on the return of illegal migrants.
